patches.old_text: ACH Direct Debit lets US businesses pull funds from customers' US bank accounts. API enum: `us_bank_account`. Business-initiated, delayed notification, reusable. Not guaranteed — disputes and payment failures possible.
patches.new_text: ACH Direct Debit lets eligible businesses in the documented US and European locations pull funds from customers' US bank accounts, with Canada labeled private preview in the 2026-11-07 capture. API enum: `us_bank_account`. USD presentment, delayed notification, reusable, and not guaranteed — disputes and payment failures remain possible. Account and industry eligibility require separate confirmation.
patches.reason: Correct the US-only merchant claim while keeping US customer and USD payment scope distinct.
warnings: Dated availability is not individual-account eligibility.

patches.old_text: Custom payment forms must display mandate text. Stripe emails mandate confirmation + microdeposit notification to customer's billing email.
patches.new_text: Custom Payment Intents forms must display mandate terms before confirmation. Nacha requires an electronic or hard copy of the mandate. With a billing email, Stripe defaults to sending mandate confirmation and, if microdeposit verification is needed, its verification notification. Custom notification flows also require microdeposit reminders.
patches.reason: Make default delivery conditional on billing email and microdeposit need, and distinguish Nacha's mandate-copy rule from email delivery.

patches.old_text: **Proof of Authorization inquiry**: upload evidence via Dashboard or Files API; `charge.dispute.created` with `warning_needs_response` status.
patches.new_text: **Proof of Authorization inquiry**: when Stripe requests proof before the bank decides a late return, `charge.dispute.created` can carry `warning_needs_response`; submit authorization evidence only on request and only once via Dashboard or Files API. This inquiry is not an appeal of a final ACH dispute.
patches.reason: Separate a requested predecision inquiry from uncontestable final disputes.

patches.new_text:
- 2026-11-07 capture: asynchronous full refunds, up to 3 business days to complete; partial refunds marked unsupported. The 2026-05-02 capture instead listed partial refunds supported and at least 3 business days to process.

> [!warning] Contradiction
> The two dated ACH captures disagree on partial-refund support and the direction of the three-business-day timing. Neither establishes an effective change date or behavior for a specific historical payment; verify the account and payment before promising either.
patches.reason: Correct the retained minimum-time claim and expose the material dated conflict.
warnings: Source captures do not resolve live account eligibility or old-transaction behavior.

patches.old_text:
- First dispute: mandate invalidated (must collect new mandate)
- Second dispute: bank account blocked entirely
patches.new_text:
- A disputed payment invalidates the mandate associated with that PaymentMethod. Resolve the dispute with the customer and collect a new mandate before attempting another charge with it.
- If a subsequent payment from the same bank account is disputed, Stripe blocks that bank account from further reuse.
patches.reason: Scope the first-dispute effect to the disputed PaymentMethod and the later block to a subsequent disputed payment from the same bank account, consistent with the accepted ACH acceptance candidate.
warnings: Overlaps the accepted ACH accept-a-payment candidate's dispute concept correction; coordinator must merge once.

patches.old_text: **Currency**: USD only. **Country**: US customers; 33+ business countries.
patches.new_text: **Presentment currency**: USD. **Settlement**: the 2026-11-07 capture lists local-currency settlement for eligible merchant Stripe accounts. **Customer location**: US; business locations include the listed European countries and US, with Canada in private preview.
patches.reason: Separate USD presentment from eligible merchant local-currency settlement, correcting the unqualified USD-only claim.
warnings: Dated page support is not account-specific eligibility.

patches.old_text: Stripe blocks accounts on certain ACH returns. Listen for `payment_method.automatically_updated` event; check `us_bank_account.status_details.blocked`. Block removed event signals account is usable again.
patches.new_text: Stripe can block bank accounts on certain ACH returns. Listen for `payment_method.automatically_updated` and inspect `us_bank_account.status_details.blocked`. When Stripe removes a block, the payment method can be reused only if an active mandate exists or a new one is collected.
patches.reason: Correct the implication that block removal alone restores authorization to debit.

patches.old_text:
- First dispute: mandate invalidated (must collect new mandate)
- Second dispute: bank account blocked entirely
patches.new_text:
- A disputed payment revokes authorization on that PaymentMethod. Reusing it requires resolving the dispute with the customer and obtaining authorization again; see the 2026-05-02 [[source-stripe-ach-accept-payment]] guide.
- Stripe says it blocks the same bank account after more than one disputed payment from that bank account. This is a same-bank-account threshold, not a universal second-dispute rule.
patches.reason: The current concept overstates both the first-dispute object and the second-dispute threshold. Old guide lines 413 and 424–444 qualify them. The November base-URL index contains no dispute mechanics.
warnings: Historical 2026-05-02 guide only; the November index does not establish current dispute behavior.

patches.new_text: | TEL | Telephone-Initiated | Oral authorization over phone; November 7, 2026 capture labels private preview; single entries only, no standing or recurring TEL entries |
patches.reason: New:51-57 labels TEL private preview and limits TEL to single entries. The current concept table retains private beta (old:84-90).
warnings: Private preview is a captured availability label; merchant account access is unverified.

patches.old_text: PPD requires `mandate_data.customer_acceptance.type: 'offline'` + `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options.collection_method: 'paper'`. TEL requires an existing customer relationship and captured oral authorization (recording or prior written notice).
patches.new_text:
PPD requires offline customer acceptance and `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options.collection_method: 'paper'` in the captured examples. For TEL, the November guide permits either a qualifying direct existing merchant-customer relationship **or**, without one, a customer-initiated telephone call; an affiliate-only relationship does not qualify. It also requires commercially reasonable identity and routing-number verification and explicit oral authorization containing online-mandate information and a customer inquiry number. Capture that authorization through an audio recording (subject to applicable recording law) or written notice **before the first debit**; the guide's sample wording is not prescribed verbatim. See [[source-stripe-ach-sec-codes]].

> [!warning] Contradiction: the previous concept said TEL was private beta and universally required an existing relationship. The November 7, 2026 capture labels it private preview and includes the customer-initiated-call alternative. Neither capture proves access for a particular account.
patches.reason: Both old:94-115 and new:61-82 allow the customer-initiated-call alternative, require separate verification and authorization content, and distinguish recording from written notice before first debit. The prior concept overstates existing-relationship necessity and omits the authorization conditions.
warnings: TEL requirements are separate from PPD offline acceptance; preview access is not established.

patches.old_text: Standard Entry Class (SEC) codes define how a customer authorized the transaction. Stripe defaults to WEB (consumers) and CCD (businesses).
patches.new_text: Standard Entry Class (SEC) codes define how a customer authorized the transaction. **When no mandate collection method is specified**, the captured Stripe guide says WEB is the default for consumer bank accounts and CCD for business bank accounts.
patches.reason: Both captures explicitly condition WEB/CCD defaults on no mandate collection method being specified (old:12; new:13); current concept line 99 omits that condition.

patches.old_text: | PPD | Prearranged Payment and Deposit | Written/signed consumer authorization; requires `collection_method: 'paper'` |
patches.new_text: | PPD | Prearranged Payment and Deposit | Standing or single-entry consumer authorization in writing, signed **or otherwise authenticated**; provide a copy to the customer; the captured PPD mandate flow uses `collection_method: 'paper'` |
patches.reason: Both captures say PPD authorization is in writing and signed or otherwise authenticated, with a copy provided to the customer (old:24-28; new:25-29). Current concept line 105 reads as signature-only; retain the paper mandate option.
